forward_notes: THE c15 SEQUENCING WORKED AND IS NOW CHEAP TO KEEP. Taking c15 as the first invoke after the apply cost nothing and produced cold 3 of 3 on the first attempt, where last round's order-literal sequencing cost two failed reads and a 925 s idle. The order still lists c15 LAST in its reported set, so every executor has to rediscover this. One line in the order -- 'take c15 FIRST, before any other deployed read' -- would close it permanently. Note the amended cell no longer REQUIRES cold, so nothing breaks if it is taken late; what is lost is the cold measurement itself, which is the only reason the cell exists.

/peers HAS NO SEGMENT INSTRUMENTATION, so 'time /peers per segment' cannot be satisfied by any executor. Row Z-S353. The total is healthy (136.83 ms worst against a 5,000 ms bar) and at-3's per-member read did not make the route expensive, so nothing is urgent -- but the diagnostic question the phrasing reaches for, WHERE the time goes across 12 parallel member reads, is unanswerable until the handler emits AMGT_SEGMENT lines the way the day route does. Five emit sites already exist in scoped_amgt.py, so this is wiring, not new machinery. Until then an order should ask for the TOTAL on N names, which is measurable, and say so.

A FORWARD LIST OF READ PATHS IS NOT A DENOMINATOR, and this round is the demonstration. Both halves listed five new S3 read paths and all five were correct; the subtraction still found two store-shaped literals nobody had enumerated (row Z-S352), one of them a prefix this role's grant was DELIBERATELY STRIPPED of at AMGT-rk-91 M2. Both turned out unreachable from the request path -- so the halves were right, but right by reachability rather than by having checked. The subtraction costs one script: parse the granted prefixes out of the .tf for one denominator, extract slash-bearing literals from the changed and added files for the other, and print what is in the second and not the first. Worth making a standing step on any round that ADDS modules, which is exactly when an enumeration lapses silently.

A DEAD CONSTANT NAMING A DELIBERATELY-UNGRANTED PREFIX IS A TRAP FOR THE NEXT CALLER, not just for a least-privilege pass. roster.py ships FILINGS_PREFIX = 'filings/v1/' and POOL_BUCKET, both defined and never read, and the module's own docstring still describes reading filings/v1/<security_key>/<accession>.source.json as 'rj-6's INTERFACE'. The next person to wire a reader off that constant gets an AccessDenied that looks like a data problem -- the Z-S346 shape. Deleting two unused lines is a smaller act than the incident they invite.
